newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks zoom to record close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks zoom to record close.

text.p: Mexican stocks extended earlier gains to chalk up a new record close on Tuesday after foreign investors flooded the market to buy stocks and on expectations primary interest rates were about to fall to their lowest level since the December 1994 peso devaluation crisis, traders said.
"Foreigners entered the market in droves, floor activity was really heavy today," a trader from the Arka brokerage said.
The leading IPC share index ended up 70.90 points, or 1.93 percent, at 3,750.03.
Volume was heavy at 164 million shares traded, even after discounting cross trades, and reflected heavy dealing activity.

A Reuters survey of nine money market traders predicted an average assignment rate of 20.30 percent for bellwether 28-day Cetes at the central bank's weekly primary auction of government securities. This would be a fall of 115 basis points since last week's auction.
Analysts also put the rally down to a recovery by market heavyweight Telmex shares and positive technical signals.
Telmex L shares ended up 48 centavos at 15.24 pesos, while its ADRs gained 1 to 39.
Dealers noted Telmex had opened down 34 centavos at 14.52 pesos on a cool reaction to its fourth quarter earnings, posted after the close of trade on Monday.
"Opinions seem to be quite at variance on Telmex. Most were surprised by the report, but it was grist for the mill for a brave few," one trader said.
"Forecast sharp falls in primary rates and a more forthright entry of foreigners improved trading," said Leonor Gonzalez, a technical analyst at BBV-Probursa brokerage.
Dealers said increased participation by international investors could be seen in benchmark 48-hour peso contracts, which closed 0.4 of a peso firmer at 7.7900/7.7935 per dollar.
Technical analysts noted the IPC broke resistance at 3,700 points in late trade and probed 3,750 points by the close.
"We might see more profit-taking, but some stocks' multiples have lagged the market and a favorable outlook for fourth quarter earnings could take the bourse to new highs," one analyst said.
On the broad market, 122 stocks traded, of which gainers trounced decliners by 78 to 22.
Dealers noted that the declines list was topped by shares whose prices had moved after thin-volume deals that did not accurately reflect market or sectoral trends during the session.
